business.title: Adaptable battery charging and management system with chemistry detection and IoT integration
business.description: This paper introduces the design and implementation of a microcontroller-based battery charging and management system capable of identifying the cell chemistry and applying appropriate charging parameters. This is made possible by developing an algorithm that can identify cell chemistry by analyzing the discharge curve and classifying the cell accordingly. The paper further explains the process of categorization. The algorithm implemented differentiates between conventional lithium-ion (NMC, NCA, LCO), LFP, and NiMH battery chemistries. It was experimentally validated to be accurate without any prior identification provided by the user. The deployed system is also capable of implementing general battery management features, such as over-current protection, under-voltage protection while discharging, and over-voltage protection during charging. An IoT platform was designed to allow users to set the operational parameters and monitor, display, and analyze the results. The results show the cell chemistry determination to be accurate. The proposed system is low-cost and scalable due to its reliance on microcontrollers and algorithms.

business.title: Nanoplastic detection and quantification in high-altitude glacial snow samples from Italy, Switzerland and France
business.description: Plastic pollution is an ever-growing concern around the globe, with current research portraying the presence of contaminants even in previously pristine regions. Especially small particles, micro- and nanoplastics, can be dispersed over long stretches by atmospheric transport, reaching even the most remote areas of the planet. This study aims to portray current levels of nanoplastic contamination (< 1 μm) by analyzing snow samples from high-altitude glaciers in the European Alps (2300–3800 m) via TD-PTR-MS. We were able to detect six common plastic pollutants, with PE and PP contributing over 60% of the total mass concentration measured across all sites. On average, nanoplastic concentrations of 85 ng mL− 1 (range: 3.6 ± 12 ng mL− 1 – 470 ± 76 ng mL− 1) were detected at sampled glacier surfaces. Access to these remote regions was enabled through a citizen-science initiative, involving trained mountaineers for sample collection. The results were applied to atmospheric modelling, highlighting possible point sources of contamination. While agriculture and local plastic factories were revealed as potential sources of nanoplastics, spatial and temporal limitations complicated comparison inside the sample cluster.

science.title: The combined associations of depression and anxiety symptoms on medical students’ suicide attitudes: a network analysis
science.description: Although previous studies have examined the combined associations of depressive and anxiety symptoms on the suicide attitudes of medical students, the number of such investigations is extremely limited. These studies have predominantly employed correlational analyses to conduct a preliminary exploration, which fails to elucidate the intricate relationship between depressive and anxiety symptoms and suicide attitudes. Moreover, these approaches do not adequately identify the core symptoms or dimensions that influence suicide attitudes. The network analysis utilized in the present study addresses these limitations associated with correlational analyses. This study employed the Suicide Attitude Questionnaire, Self-Rating Depression Scale, and Self-Rating Anxiety Scale to investigate 1,667 first- and second-year medical students at a medical university. Regression analysis and network analysis were combined to explore the joint associations of depression and anxiety on medical students’ suicide attitudes. The results indicated that anxiety was significantly associated with suicide attitudes among medical students, while the dimension of depressive disorders (DD) exhibited the highest centrality in the interaction network of depression, anxiety, and suicide attitudes, serving as the core hub node with the most prominent connection strength to psychomotor disorders (PD). The study indicates that depression, anxiety, and suicide attitudes among medical students are characterized by complex multidimensional associations, with depressive disorders acting as the central hub in their interactions. These findings provide scientific evidence and specific targets for medical universities to implement precision mental health interventions, suicide prevention, and life education programs.

science.title: Decoding birth intervals for educational attainment in sibling sequences: evidence from nationally representative surveys in China
science.description: Leveraging data from three nationally representative surveys in China (N = 99,352), we investigate how birth intervals shape educational attainment. Utilizing a family fixed-effect model to minimize confounding factors, our findings illuminate a distinctive pattern: the birth interval preceding the index person correlates with enhanced educational attainment; the impact of the preceding birth interval is more pronounced for families with more than three children; but surprisingly, the birth interval following the index person shows no substantive impact on educational attainment. These robust results, supported by various validation methods and controls, not only contribute to the broader discourse on birth intervals but also offer empirical insights crucial for informed family planning decisions in China.

science.title: A global dataset of multiple meteorological drought indices for 1961-2100
science.description: Meteorological drought, characterized by atmospheric water deficit, poses widespread threats to ecosystems, agriculture, and water resources. While the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI), Evaporative Demand Drought Index (EDDI), and Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) are established monitoring tools, the scarcity of global-scale, long-term future projection datasets limits our capacity to assess drought risks in a warming world. Here we develop a new Global Meteorological Drought Dataset (GHM_drought) at 0.5° spatial resolution for the period 1961–2100, derived from the Climatic Research Unit (CRU) dataset and 16 bias-corrected Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) models. This dataset calculates SPI, EDDI, and SPEI based on a unified framework, ensuring consistency and comparability among the indices. Additionally, the dataset provides multiple accumulation timescales (1, 3, 6, 9, 12 months, and 1 year) and multiple scenarios, including historical (1961–2024) and future Shared Socioeconomic Pathway (SSP) scenarios (2025–2100) (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP5-8.5). Crucially, the dataset provides uncertainty ranges for future projections to enhance reliability. Validation results demonstrate that the GHM_drought captures historical drought events robustly and maintains high consistency with existing benchmark datasets. For future projections, the applied threshold-based quantile mapping method effectively corrects systematic biases. The GHM_drought aids global drought monitoring and projection, thereby supporting climate risk assessment and adaptation.

science.title: Immune niche composed of C1Q+ macrophages/SFRP2+ CAFs/CD8+ T cells drives immunotherapy response in HER2-positive gastric cancer
science.description: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) expression is a distinctive feature of a subgroup of gastric cancer (GC) but the underpinning characteristics of the immune microenvironment and mechanisms remain unclear. In the study, spatial transcriptomics and single-cell RNA sequencing are used on treatment-naïve HER2-positive and HER2-negative GC specimens to characterize the tumor microenvironment and spatial architecture with the aim of defining how HER2 status shapes the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) and its cellular interactions. We find that C1Q⁺ macrophages spatially and functionally interact with CD8⁺ T cells via Galectin-9 (LGALS9), which is downregulated in HER2-positive tumors. Knocking down LGALS9 enhancesCD8⁺ T cell function and suppresses tumor growth in a CD8⁺ T cell-dependent manner, further amplified by anti-PD-1 treatment. Conversely, SFRP2⁺ cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAF) promote CD8⁺ T cell exhaustion through CXCL12-CXCR4 signaling, and knocking down CXCL12 reverses this immunosuppressive effect. HER2-positive tumors are characterized by an immune-favorable niche enriched in C1Q⁺ macrophages and CD8⁺ T effector memory cells but a decrease in SFRP2⁺ CAFs, suggesting its potential as a predictive biomarker for response to combined anti-PD-1 and anti-HER2 therapies. These findings provide insight into the spatial and immune landscape of HER2-associated GC and may inform future precision treatment strategies. HER2-positive gastric cancers represent a distinct subtype of the disease showing favourable response to combination therapy involving HER2 targeting and immune checkpoint blockade immunotherapy. Here the authors show by spatial transcriptomics and single-cell RNA sequencing that HER2 positivity associates with a favourable immune microenvironment that also determines their better response to immunotherapy.
